questions.stem: In a SWOT analysis, which two elements are internal?
options: Strengths and weaknesses
Opportunities and threats
Strengths and opportunities
Weaknesses and threats
questions.why: Strengths and weaknesses are about the business itself. Opportunities and threats are about the environment it operates in.
whyNot: Those are the external elements.
One internal and one external.
One internal and one external.

questions.stem: A new competitor opens nearby. In a SWOT analysis this is:
options: a threat
a weakness
an opportunity
a strength
questions.why: It is external: it would be true whether or not this particular business existed. The weakness would be having no differentiation to defend with.
whyNot: A weakness is internal. Confusing the two is the most common error on this topic.
It damages rather than helps the business.
It is not an advantage the business possesses.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be classified as a weakness?
options: The business depends entirely on one booking platform
Visitor numbers to the region are growing
Three new competitors are opening
Platform commission rates are rising
questions.why: Dependence on one channel is a characteristic of the business itself, which it could change. That makes it internal.
whyNot: External, and helpful, so an opportunity.
External and harmful, so a threat.
External and harmful, so a threat.

questions.stem: What is the test for whether an item is internal or external?
options: Whether the business could change it directly
Whether it is helpful or harmful
Whether it involves money
Whether it is happening now or in the future
questions.why: If the business can change it, it is internal. If it would still be true whether or not this business existed, it is external.
whyNot: That decides strength against weakness, or opportunity against threat, not internal against external.
Financial items appear in all four boxes.
Timing does not determine the category.

questions.stem: Which pairing in a SWOT analysis usually identifies the greatest danger?
options: A weakness combined with a threat
A strength combined with an opportunity
A strength combined with a threat
A weakness combined with an opportunity
questions.why: This is where businesses fail: a vulnerability meeting an external pressure. Identifying that combination early is where a SWOT earns its keep.
whyNot: That is the obvious strategic move, not a danger.
The strength is what lets you defend against the threat.
The opportunity exists and cannot currently be taken, which is frustrating rather than dangerous.

questions.stem: Why can the same fact be both a strength and a weakness?
options: A specialised efficient factory is a strength while demand holds and a weakness when the market shifts
SWOT analyses are always wrong
Facts change over time
Managers cannot agree on definitions
questions.why: Context decides. Specialisation gives low cost and no flexibility, so it helps or hurts depending on what happens to demand. Saying this is a high-level evaluation point.
whyNot: Overstated; they are subjective rather than always wrong.
The fact has not changed; its significance has.
Disagreement about definitions is a different problem.

questions.stem: What is the main limitation of a SWOT analysis?
options: It lists items without prioritising or weighting them
It cannot include external factors
It requires financial data to complete
It can only be used by large businesses
questions.why: Twenty items with no weighting is not a strategy. The framework does not tell you which threat actually matters most.
whyNot: Opportunities and threats are precisely the external half.
Much of a SWOT is qualitative.
It is widely used by small businesses.

questions.stem: Why is 'strong brand' a weak entry in a SWOT analysis?
options: It is not specific or evidenced, so it cannot be acted on
Branding is not an internal factor
Brands are always weaknesses
SWOT analyses cannot include marketing items
questions.why: Compare it with 'highest review score on the island at 9.1'. Specific and evidenced entries can be paired with opportunities and turned into a strategy; vague ones cannot.
whyNot: A brand is an internal asset, so the classification is right. The problem is vagueness.
A strong brand is a genuine strength.
Marketing items belong in a SWOT.

questions.stem: How should a SWOT analysis be used in an exam answer?
options: Classify items from the source, then pair them to suggest a strategy
List as many items as possible in each box
Describe what a SWOT analysis is
Focus only on the strengths
questions.why: The classification earns little. Saying 'this strength applied to this opportunity suggests this strategy' is where the analysis and evaluation marks are.
whyNot: Length without prioritisation is the framework's main weakness.
Description is knowledge only.
A one-sided analysis misses the point of the tool.
